c74object.name: bachmcp.onnxb~
c74object.digest: Hear a buffer~ with a sound model
c74object.description: Runs a sound model of models/audio/ on a buffer~: a tagger (CED) names what it hears with AudioSet labels and scores, a CLAP (LAION CLAP, CLAP2) compares the sound with texts or gives its embedding. The same models the bach-mcp server uses, as ONNX: download them with python py/main.py download <name>. On bang the channels of source are mixed, resampled to the model's rate and heard on a worker thread, never Max's; the answer comes later, as dictionary <name> out of the left outlet, then a bang out of the right one. A sound longer than window is heard in up to windows windows spread over it: a tagger keeps each label's highest score, a CLAP the mean of the embeddings. Objects loading the same model share it. Apple Silicon only; ONNX Runtime comes with python py/main.py install (into support/), and bachmcp.onnx~ must sit next to this object.

method.name: bang
method.description: Hears source from start to end with the model of model. Nothing comes out at once: when the analysis is done, the left outlet sends dictionary <name> and the right outlet a bang. A bang sent while an analysis runs waits its turn.

method.name: source
method.description: The same as source: the next bang hears this buffer~.

attribute.name: model
attribute.description: A sound model name of models/catalog.toml (in models/audio/), or a model folder's full path. Taggers: ced-base, ced-mini (16 kHz, 10 s). LAION CLAP: laion-clap-music-speech, laion-clap-general, laion-clap-small (48 kHz, 10 s). CLAP2: laion-clap2-m, laion-clap2-l (32 kHz, 30 s). It loads on a worker thread; when it is ready the right outlet says model <name> <kind> <samplerate> <window>.

attribute.name: source
attribute.description: The buffer~ heard on bang. Its channels are mixed into one (their mean), as the bach-mcp server hears a buffer; its own sample rate is resampled to the model's.

attribute.name: start
attribute.description: Where in source to start hearing, in ms.

attribute.name: end
attribute.description: Where in source to stop hearing, in ms. 0 (default): the end of the buffer~.

attribute.name: window
attribute.description: How many seconds the model hears at once. 0 (default): the model's own (10 s; CLAP2 30 s). A LAION CLAP hears 10 s at most: a longer window is cut, with a warning.

attribute.name: windows
attribute.description: A sound longer than window is heard in up to this many windows, spread evenly over it (first and last included). Tags keep each label's highest score; a CLAP takes the mean of the windows' embeddings.

attribute.name: samplerate
attribute.digest: Sample rate fed to the model (Hz)
attribute.description: 0 (default): the model's own rate (16000 CED, 48000 LAION CLAP, 32000 CLAP2); the sound is resampled to it here. Any other rate is used as given, with a warning: the model was trained at its own rate and its answers may be wrong.

attribute.name: labels
attribute.description: A tagger's answer has at most this many labels, the highest scores first.

attribute.name: threshold
attribute.description: A tagger leaves out labels scoring below this (scores are 0-1). If none reaches it, tags is empty.

attribute.name: text
attribute.description: Each atom is one text (quote texts with spaces: "A drum loop plays." "A man is speaking."). They are embedded once, when set or when the model loads; each answer then says, in this order, the cosine between the sound and each text (about -1 to 1; higher is closer, and only the order between texts means much). LAION's CLAPs were trained on captions: full sentences work better than single words. A tagger ignores it, with a warning.

attribute.name: embedding
attribute.description: 1: a CLAP's answer also holds the sound's embedding, a unit vector (512 numbers for LAION CLAP, 640 CLAP2-M, 960 CLAP2-L), to compare sounds with each other. A CLAP with no text and embedding 0 has nothing to say, and warns so.

c74object.discussion: The answer is a dictionary the object owns, filled again at each answer: copy it (dict) to keep it. Its keys: model and kind (tagger, clap, clap2); samplerate, the Hz the model was fed; duration, the ms heard; source, start, end (ms), what was heard; a tagger's tags, an array of { label, score }, highest first; a CLAP's similarity, an array of { text, score } in text order, and embedding with embedding 1.
